# Bar table

Contents: [Use cases](#use-cases), [Chart IDs](#chart-ids), [Minimal spec](#minimal-spec), [Data](#data), [Options](#options), [Annotations](#annotations), [Sizing](#sizing), [Fixtures](#fixtures), [Not for](#not-for).

<!-- Generated by scripts/generate-reference.mjs from the boardplot describe, list and fixtures payloads. -->

Table rows with number columns and stacked bars. One panel when the rows compare one measure (impact in $bn, split into Run and Grow); several panels when the same split reads in different units side by side ($bn and % of EBITDA). Each panel has its own scale; the end label is the row total or an authored range, whose bar fills the segments to low and extends lightly to high. variant 'cascade': panels as periods of one total (category share by year). Type `bartable`. Aliases: `bar-table`, `table-bars`.

## Use cases

- One measure per row as a stacked bar beside number columns: one panel
- The same split in two units side by side, $bn and % of EBITDA: two panels
- Impact ranges by sector with a Total row
- Share of a total over 2 to 4 periods, such as category revenue share by year: cascade

## Chart IDs

- `bartable.panels`: fixture `impact-two-panels-named-share`
- `bartable.cascade`: fixture `cascade-two-periods`

## Minimal spec

```json
{
  "type": "bartable",
  "data": {
    "categories": [{ "id": "sw", "label": "Software" }, { "id": "ut", "label": "Utilities" }],
    "series": [{ "id": "run", "label": "Run" }, { "id": "grow", "label": "Grow" }],
    "columns": [{ "id": "n", "label": "# of companies", "values": [30, 45], "format": "1,234" }],
    "panels": [
      {
        "id": "abs",
        "label": "EBITDA impact",
        "unit": "$bn",
        "weight": 2,
        "values": { "run": [40, 30], "grow": [100, 75] },
        "ends": [{ "low": 110, "high": 160 }, { "low": 80, "high": 160 }]
      },
      {
        "id": "pct",
        "label": "Share of 2030 EBITDA",
        "unit": "%",
        "weight": 1,
        "aggregate": "none",
        "values": { "run": [8, 9], "grow": [26, 30] },
        "ends": [{ "low": 28, "high": 40 }, { "low": 29, "high": 60 }]
      }
    ]
  },
  "options": {
    "total": true,
    "title": "Software and utilities carry half of the upside",
    "subtitle": { "measure": "Estimated 2030 EBITDA run-rate impact" },
    "source": "Illustrative model"
  }
}
```

## Data

| Path | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| categories | array | yes | The rows, top to bottom. |
| categories[].id | string | yes | Row identity; not __total, which names the Total row. |
| categories[].label | string |  | Row name in the label column; defaults to the id. Long names wrap to two lines. |
| categories[].group | string |  | Row group id from data.rowGroups: the bar takes its colour. Required under rowGroups, except on a residual row. |
| categories[].residual | boolean |  | A rest row ("Rest of world"): neutral grey, pinned below the other rows. |
| series | array | yes | The segments of every bar, left to right. Two or more draw a key; one draws none and the panel head names the measure. |
| series[].id | string | yes | Segment identity; every panel keys its values by it. |
| series[].label | string |  | Segment name in the key; defaults to the id. |
| series[].colorRole | string |  | Theme colour role for this segment when no fill is set. One of good, bad, warn, neutral, neutralLight, highlight, total, others; series-N for step N of the theme ramp, 1-based (series-2 is color.series[1]); or status-<key> for a theme status colour. A hex colour goes in fill. |
| series[].fill | string |  | Explicit CSS fill for this segment. |
| columns | array |  | Number columns between the row labels and the panels, such as a count per row. Zero or more. |
| columns[].id | string | yes | Column identity; distinct from every panel id. |
| columns[].label | string |  | Column head, right-aligned over the numbers; wraps to two lines. |
| columns[].values | array | yes | One number per row, in row order; null prints the missing glyph, { state } n/a or n.m. |
| columns[].values[].state | string | yes | 'na' prints n/a, 'nm' prints n.m. One of `'na'`, `'nm'`. |
| columns[].format | string |  | Format by example, such as 1,234 or 12.5%. |
| columns[].aggregate | string |  | What the Total row prints: 'sum' (default) adds the column, 'none' leaves the cell empty for numbers that do not add up, such as averages or rates. One of `'sum'`, `'none'`. |
| panels | array | yes | One stacked-bar panel per measure, each with its own unit and scale. Use one panel when the rows compare one measure: EBITDA impact in $bn, split into Run and Grow. Use several when the same split reads in different units side by side: the impact in $bn and the same impact as % of EBITDA. Bars in different panels compare by length only under sharedScale true. Under variant 'cascade' the panels are periods of one total. |
| panels[].id | string | yes | Panel identity; distinct from every column id. |
| panels[].label | string |  | The measure, printed in the head as "label, unit". |
| panels[].unit | string |  | Unit of this panel, such as $bn or %; printed in the head, never in the end labels. |
| panels[].weight | number |  | Share of the width left for the panels; default 1. A weight of 2 beside 1 gives the first panel two thirds. |
| panels[].values | object | yes | Segment id -> one value per row, in row order. Every segment in data.series appears, and every key is a segment id. |
| panels[].values.*[].state | string | yes | 'na' prints n/a, 'nm' prints n.m. One of `'na'`, `'nm'`. |
| panels[].ends | array |  | Per row, in row order: a range for the row total, or null for none. A row with a range draws its segments to low, each keeping its share of the segments' sum, then a light outlined extension from low to high, and prints "low–high" after it. So the segment values set the split only: Run 40 and Grow 100 with a range of 110–160 draw, hover and list in the data table as about 31 and 79, their parts of 110. A row without a range draws and prints its sum. The Total row adds the ranges, counting a row without one at its sum at both ends. |
| panels[].ends[].low | number | yes | Lower end of the row total, where the segments end; zero or more. |
| panels[].ends[].high | number | yes | Upper end of the row total, where the light extension ends; at least low. |
| panels[].format | string |  | Format by example for the end labels and the total; falls back to options.format. |
| panels[].aggregate | string |  | What the Total row prints for this panel: 'sum' (default) adds the rows, or their ranges when a row has one; 'none' leaves it empty. Use 'none' for shares, rates or averages, such as a % of each row's own base, whose sum means nothing. One of `'sum'`, `'none'`. |
| rowGroups | object |  | Colour bars by a row attribute, keyed under a title. Needs one segment. |
| rowGroups.title | string |  | Key title with the unit ("Margin of market, %"). |
| rowGroups.groups | array | yes | In key order. |
| rowGroups.groups[].id | string | yes | Group identity; rows name it in group. |
| rowGroups.groups[].label | string |  | Name in the key; defaults to the id. |
| rowGroups.groups[].colorRole | string |  | Theme colour role when no fill is set. One of good, bad, warn, neutral, neutralLight, highlight, total, others; series-N for step N of the theme ramp, 1-based (series-2 is color.series[1]); or status-<key> for a theme status colour. A hex colour goes in fill. |
| rowGroups.groups[].fill | string |  | Explicit CSS fill. |

## Options

| Path | Type | Values | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| total | boolean |  | `true` | Closing Total row, labelled with strings.total; default true. Summed number columns print their sum; a panel prints the summed ranges when a row has one (a row without counts its sum at both ends), else the sum of the bars, as text without a bar. |
| combinedShare | object |  |  | A note with the combined share of these rows in each summed panel: their sum over the panel's, at the low and the high end where rows carry ranges ('Core segments: 120 of 300 $bn at the low end, 40%; 210 of 500 at the high end, 42%'). A row id that names no row is refused. |
| combinedShare.rows | array |  |  | Row ids whose combined share prints; at least two, each once. |
| combinedShare.label | string |  |  | What the rows are called together in the note; default their labels joined with 'and'. |
| variant | string | `'panels'`, `'cascade'` |  | 'panels' (default): one stacked-bar panel per measure. 'cascade': share cascade, each panel splits its total; a row starts where the row above ended, on a light track over the total. The Total row is a dark bar. combinedShare draws a bracket over its rows, which must follow one another. Needs one segment, no ends, no nulls. |
| cascade | object |  |  | Settings of variant 'cascade'; refused with variant 'panels'. |
| cascade.share | boolean |  |  | Computed share column beside each panel; default true. rounding defaults to 'sum-consistent' here, so each adds up to 100%. |
| cascade.growth | object |  |  | Growth column after the last panel. |
| cascade.growth.measure | string | `'cagr'`, `'share-change'` |  | 'cagr': each row's CAGR, first panel to last, in %. 'share-change': last share minus first, in pp. |
| cascade.growth.years | number |  |  | Years from first to last panel for 'cagr'; default read from the panel labels (2019, FY24). |
| cascade.growth.label | string |  |  | Column head; default from the panel labels. |
| sharedScale | boolean |  |  | false: each panel its own scale. true: one scale, panel width follows its longest bar; weights refused. Default false, true under cascade. |

Plus the [shared options](options.md). This type does not accept `detailFields`, `labels`, `categoryLabels`, `valueAxis`, `categoryAxis`, `secondaryAxis`, `rowLabels`, `sort`, `topN`, `bandFraction`, `hatchStrength`, `colorblindSafe`.

## Annotations

This type takes no annotations.

## Sizing

Floor 280 × 28 px; fit `content`.

Below the floor a render is refused with `size-below-floor` and the pixels it needs. `measure` returns the natural and comfortable size for a given spec; see [Sizing in the manual](../manual.md#sizing).

|---|---|---|
| impact-two-panels | torture | Two panels, one split: the impact in $bn and as a share of EBITDA, with a count column and a Total row |

| cascade-four-years | example | Share cascade over four years: product-category revenue share with the share change in pp |

## Not for

Values of different sign: bars grow from zero. Comparing bars of different units by length: each panel has its own scale.
